title: The 2023 ASASSN-14ko UV data permit one nonlinear colour relation within reported error boxes
abstract: Do the 2023 UV colours of ASASSN-14ko require different rise and decline branches? A prior affine colour test failed, but a nonlinear relation can also fail that test. We give a graph test for a common nondecreasing curve through two-band error boxes. It tests both measured coordinates and allows any nonlinear shape. All 25 XMM-Newton imaging visits admit such a curve with each coordinate moved by at most 0.770 of its reported error. With 1-percent added error the limit is 0.699; an affine relation needs 1.921. Fast-mode photometry needs 1.728 with reported errors alone. A monotone cubic has chi-square 50.84 with reported errors and 21.22 with 2-percent added error, for 21 nominal residual degrees of freedom. Thus the unrestricted result depends on curve flexibility. The data do not require multiple UV branches under this error-box test. This does not show that the spectrum is fixed, that the response is instantaneous, or that the physical clock is orbital. We supply a proof, tested code, source hashes, aggregate results and a retrieval recipe. Observation tables remain external.

display.caption: A common nondecreasing curve passes through the UV error boxes. The curve is a feasibility example, not a physical spectral fit. The smooth cubic is a separate diagnostic.
